review.summary: The prior MAJOR looks fixed in the supplied component. When the result is ready or needs_attention, the video, start-time and title fields are disabled, the submit button is not rendered, and the only way to start a new intent is "建立另一場" (Create another). That button does a full document navigation to /lives/new, which loads a fresh server request ID and fresh hook state. Pending and error states still keep the same ID and field values, as intended. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR in this scope. Two smaller items remain: one untested path where browser Back might bring back an editable form with the old ID (MINOR, low confidence), and the navigation being a button instead of a link (NIT). The updated browser test hasn't run yet, so this review doesn't confirm that the tests or release pass.

findings.file: fast-entry quick webinar form component (supplied excerpt)
findings.area: `useState(requestId)` / `useActionState` initial state; completion lock depends only on client action state
findings.issue: The completion lock exists only in component state. If the page component remounts with a cached server payload, the old requestId comes back while `state` resets to idle, which would make the form editable again with the completed identity. This could happen after a soft navigation away (for example the editor or live `Link`s in the result panel) followed by browser Back, if the client router reuses that payload. The new browser assertions only cover the 'Create another' full-navigation path.
findings.evidence: `const [submissionId] = useState(requestId);` and `completed = state.status === "ready" || ...`; after a remount the state goes back to `{ status: "idle" }`. The result panel offers soft `<Link>` navigations (`state.editorUrl`, `state.liveUrl`, `state.publicUrl`). The task's browser scope covers locked completion, a second creation through 'Create another' and the project refresh, but not Link-then-Back.
findings.impact: If the cached payload is reused, a user could submit a new video or time under an already-used request ID. The idempotent server path would then silently return or keep the earlier resource, which is the same intent-collision class as the prior MAJOR. Whether this happens depends on the Next router cache, which may be cleared by `revalidatePath` in the action, so confidence is low.
findings.recommended_fix: Make sure /lives/new always gets a fresh requestId when it remounts. For example, mark the route dynamic and confirm `revalidatePath` clears the router cache, or have the server reject a reused requestId whose payload differs from the stored one, with a clear message. Alternatively, open the result links in a way that doesn't leave a restorable editable form with the old ID.
findings.required_test: Browser test: complete a creation, click 'Check page and publish settings' (soft Link), press browser Back, then assert that either the form is locked or the hidden requestId differs from the completed one. Submitting a different video must not map to the first resource.

findings.file: fast-entry quick webinar form component (supplied excerpt)
findings.issue: This is a navigation built as a `<button>` that calls `window.location.assign` with a hardcoded path. It can't be middle-clicked, opened in a new tab or have its URL copied, and it skips the basePath/locale prefixing that `Link` would add if the app ever sets them.
findings.evidence: `<button type="button" ... onClick={() => window.location.assign("/lives/new")}>建立另一場</button>`, styled with `underline` to look like a link.
findings.impact: Minor accessibility and semantics mismatch, plus a possible wrong URL under a basePath. Functionally fine with the current config.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a native `<a href="/lives/new">` with a narrowly scoped lint-disable comment that explains why full navigation is needed, or build the URL with the configured basePath if one exists. Keep it rendered only when `completed`.
findings.required_test: Existing browser assertion for 'Create another' (different URL/resource) should keep passing; optionally assert the element has the link role.
